## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

Sekhiya 65 of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, titled *Pallatthika* ("Clasping the knees"), is a training rule on proper monastic deportment found in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Within the Pali canon, SuttaCentral lists full parallels in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Sekhiya 65), the Bhikkhu Parivāra (Sekhiya 65), and the parallel nun's code in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (all Sekhiya 65) [SuttaCentral]. Extensive cross-tradition parallels are attested across other early Buddhist Vinayas, including the Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣa sūtras of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Lokottaravāda schools preserved in Chinese (e.g., Sarvāstivāda Sk 95; Mahāsāṅghika Sk 55, *Nokkuṭikaṁ nisinnassa*), Sanskrit texts and fragments, and Tibetan translations (e.g., Mūlasarvāstivāda Sk 88) [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records 85 matching passages shared with 34 other Pali texts, showing strong structural alignment with closely related Sekhiya rules governing posture and conduct, notably Sekhiyas 64, 62, 66, 70, 63, and 59 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches above its reporting threshold [DharmaNexus].
